findings.quote: If the stem said "an operator must approve each failover" instead: change weights by hand, and accept that [this is a control plane operation](../facts/route53.md#route53-dr-weight-change-is-control-plane).

findings.evidence: The cited fact route53-dr-weight-change-is-control-plane itself continues: "However, be aware this is a control plane operation and therefore not as resilient as the data plane approach using Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC)." source_id docs/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/best-practices-dns (line 9): "For scenarios such as failover during disaster recovery, we recommend that you use features like Route 53 health checks and ARC routing control that rely on data plane functionality to update DNS." The twin keeps the stem's 'even if the Route 53 control plane is impaired' and 'MOST resilient', and the same question's Why not calls the weight change less resilient; 2-deep teaches 'use only data plane operations'. findings.resolution: fix-13: q013 twin now reads: 'If the stem said "an operator must approve each failover" instead: keep the failover records and switch them with ARC routing control; AWS recommends [features like Route 53 health checks and ARC routing control that rely on data plane functionality](route53-bp-control-plane-prioritizes-consistency-not-availability).' findings.resolution: fix-13: step 4 now says 'A non-alias record [must have a TTL](route53-ttl-required-on-all-records). For an alias record to an AWS resource, [Route 53 uses the default TTL for the resource](route53-alias-to-aws-resource-ttl-not-settable).'
